scenes.title: The same naira. Counted once.
scenes.caption: Ajora · Entity resolution for multi-bank finance
scenes.voice: Your own transfer should not look like new income. Meet Ajora, a financial insights demo for Nigeria.

scenes.title: When your own money looks like income
scenes.caption: Emeka’s raw inflow: ₦6.99M across four accounts.
scenes.voice: Emeka banks across four accounts. A naive total says he earned six point nine nine million naira. Some of that money was already his.

scenes.title: Find evidence across institutions
scenes.caption: Amount + timing + references + fuzzy name similarity
scenes.voice: Ajora compares amounts, timestamps, payment references and fuzzy name similarity across banks. These features score candidate debit and credit pairs.

scenes.title: One debit. One credit.
scenes.caption: Rule-based confidence scoring + Hungarian assignment
scenes.voice: The Hungarian algorithm selects pairs globally. Each transaction can be matched only once. The current demo uses explainable rules for confidence scoring.

scenes.title: Show the evidence. Keep the user in control.
scenes.caption: High confidence → apply. Uncertain → ask. Every match can be reviewed.
scenes.voice: High confidence matches apply automatically. Uncertain pairs stay in cashflow until confirmed, and users can inspect or reject any match.

scenes.title: ₦6.99M → ₦5.60M income
scenes.caption: 8 self-transfers removed. Fees stay in spending. Net cashflow stays the same.
scenes.voice: Eight internal transfers are removed. Income becomes five point six million naira. Transfer fees remain in spending, so net cashflow stays the same.

scenes.title: Measure the matching pipeline
scenes.caption: Precision and recall on labelled demo fixtures
scenes.voice: On the bundled labelled demo data: all eighteen transfer pairs found, with no false matches. Broader validation is still needed.

scenes.title: The communal economy, made visible
scenes.caption: Graph structure + transaction cues → remittances, family support and more
scenes.voice: On the cleaned ledger, graph patterns and narration cues reveal remittances and recurring family support. Every relationship can be inspected.

scenes.title: The engine computes. The narrator explains.
scenes.caption: Offline templates in this demo. Quoted numbers checked against computed facts.
scenes.voice: The engine computes. The offline narrator explains those facts. The demo checks every quoted number against its structured inputs.

scenes.title: Revoke an account. Recalculate the view.
scenes.caption: Domiciliary account excluded → remittance disappears → figures update
scenes.voice: Revoke the domiciliary account. The remittance disappears, and the remaining figures are recalculated.

scenes.title: See what was served — and excluded
scenes.caption: Append-only access log · no database server
scenes.voice: The audit log records which accounts were served, and which were excluded by revoked consent.

scenes.title: See the financial life underneath.
scenes.caption: Try the live sample-data demo · select Persona B
scenes.voice: Try Ajora’s sample data demo. Select Persona B to explore the full story.
